rulings.target: outcomes[mortality survival rate dichotomous @not reported]
rulings.reason: Table 1 reports 'Survival rate 12/20 (60%)' for the whole cohort with no timepoint. GLM files it under the peep_pl condition arm and sets is_longest_reported_mortality, which would present a cohort figure as condition-specific mortality in a crossover. A co-author should decide whether to keep it as cohort-level mortality (needs a single-group arm; 8/20 deaths or 12/20 survivors, timepoint not_reported) or drop it from outcomes.

All 20 enrolled patients were monitored with the esophageal balloon after enrolment and all 20 contribute PL values to Table 2; GLM marks the count derived and explains it.
End-inspiratory and end-expiratory PL are reported for all 20 patients in both steps, so 20 successful placements follows from the reported data; flagged derived.

Balloon 'inflated as recommended by the manufacturer' (filling = manufacturer_recommended_volume) and position 'verified using passive chest compressions during occlusions' (a dynamic occlusion test in paralysed patients). The schema defines method as how the filling volume was chosen, while the codebook's categories imply an occlusion test takes precedence over a stated volume. A co-author needs to set which axis wins; both reviewers read the paper correctly.
Table 1 reports 'Days of intubation [before] study 3 (2-5)', an interval measured from intubation, so the reference event is intubation, not enrolment.

Median BMI 28 kg/m2 with IQR 24-33: below the obese_population threshold, but the upper quartile is obese, and the authors call the population pre-obese. mixed_bmi fits better than non_obese_population.
The EIT Silent Spaces strategy is not a transpulmonary pressure target; the study applies one Ptp strategy (positive end-expiratory PL via the sliding table).
Timing is known relative to intubation: median 3 days (IQR 2-5) of intubation before the study, so at least three quarters of patients were at or beyond 48 h: late_after_48h.
